in_text_mentions: Enlargement of the lateral ventricles, as depicted in Figure 5, is common, occurring in 94–100% of cases; in most cases, it is moderate-to-pronounced and symmetric; it is accompanied by septations in 10–29% of cases, and occipital horns are commonly seen, sometimes making it difficult to distinguish periventricular cysts(34-43). It should also be borne in mind that the presence of ventriculomegaly is directly related to a reduction in brain volume and can cause the head circumference to remain normal or even increase(34-40,43).

plate_findings.evidence: Severe microcephaly with scalp folds

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Three-dimensional reconstruction of head CT from an article on neonates with confirmed congenital Zika syndrome; the caption directly states severe microcephaly with scalp folds, the classic CZS presentation, so the panel qualifies as a real patient image showing a target-disease manifestation. Skin tone is not assessable from the grayscale volume rendering. B: Three-dimensional reconstruction of head CT showing prominent occipital bone and overlapping sutures; the caption and in-text (nine of 16 neonates, 56.2%) document this in neonates with confirmed congenital Zika syndrome, representing the collapsed-skull/fetal brain disruption sequence component of severe microcephaly, so it qualifies as a real patient image of the target disease. The specific terms prominent occipital bone and overlapping sutures are absent from the vocabulary and are listed as proposed findings.

in_text_mentions: Ventriculomegaly was observed in 15 newborns (93.7%), being supratentorial in 10 (66.7%) and global in 5 (33.3%). Colpocephaly was a common finding, seen in 10 patients (62.5%), and was associated with the parallel appearance of the lateral ventricles (50%). A: Axial CT from a child with congenital Zika syndrome showing the classic triad of punctate cortico-subcortical calcifications, cerebral atrophy with ventriculomegaly, and collapsed skull/bone overlap characteristic of fetal brain disruption sequence. in_text_mentions: b presented an extended elbow with limitation to the reduction, pronation arm, flexed wrist, non-reducible hand with cyanotic coloration. The upper right limb was conformed only to the proximal third of the arm. At this level, soft tissue defect was found with the presence of an irregular cutaneous line, exposure of subcutaneous tissue and the humeral condyle, no tissue bleeding was detected (Figure 1). The lower extremities presented limitation to hip abduction, knee extension and flexion of both feet. The genitalia anatomy showed 1 cm penis and a complete rough scrotum without testes inside.
